  "moves": [
    {
      "moveId": "pro-science-leaves-existential-questions",
      "side": "pro",
      "sectionTitle": "personal routes and epistemic scope",
      "role": "Constructive",
      "currentDescription": "Collins concludes that scientific competence does not exhaust rational inquiry because questions about purpose, death, God, and existence remain outside its direct assistance.",
      "lockedProposition": "Collins found that science did not address existential questions such as purpose, death, God, and why anything exists.",
      "completeLockedSourceExcerpt": "and then i began to realize there were questions that science wasn't helping me with like why am i here anyway what happens after you die is there a god why is there something instead of nothing and i began to realize i was a bit impoverished in the ability to approach those things",
      "assessmentRationaleWithoutScores": "Strongest feature: Collins identifies specific existential questions and draws the restrained conclusion that science was not helping him answer them, thereby opening legitimate space for additional modes of rational inquiry. Principal limitation: Scientific noncoverage supplies no positive warrant that theology answers these questions correctly, much less that God is the best explanation, so the move establishes scope rather than a theistic inference. Live burden: Collins must connect purpose, mortality, and existence to publicly assessable reasons for belief while avoiding any suggestion that an unanswered question itself favors God."
    },
    {
      "moveId": "con-darwin-replaced-design",
      "side": "con",
      "sectionTitle": "personal routes and epistemic scope",
      "role": "Constructive",
      "currentDescription": "Dawkins concludes that Darwinian evolution explains biological complexity previously attributed to design, thereby removing his former explanatory reason for positing a creator.",
      "lockedProposition": "Dawkins abandoned creator belief when Darwinian evolution explained biological complexity that had seemed to need a designer.",
      "completeLockedSourceExcerpt": "and uh so i retained a belief in some kind of creator because i felt that that level of complexity needed a designer and then when i finally understood the full magnitude of the darwinian explanation then that dropped away and and i i decided that there was no need for that not only no need for it",
      "assessmentRationaleWithoutScores": "Strongest feature: Dawkins connects a clearly identified scientific development to a proportionate autobiographical conclusion: once gradual selection explained apparent design, the designer ceased doing necessary explanatory work. Principal limitation: The passage reports the magnitude of Darwin’s achievement without presenting its mechanisms, and replacing one biological design inference does not independently settle cosmic origins, morality, transcendence, or every conception of God. Live burden: Dawkins must preserve the careful transition from “no need” in explaining biological complexity to his wider case, while answering Collins’s claim that a divine plan can remain compatible with the mechanism."
    },
    {
      "moveId": "pro-comparative-inquiry-supported-faith",
      "side": "pro",
      "sectionTitle": "personal routes and epistemic scope",
      "role": "Constructive",
      "currentDescription": "Collins concludes that faith became rationally preferable after sustained theological inquiry exposed his objections as superficial, although the decisive comparative arguments remain unstated.",
      "lockedProposition": "After encountering theological arguments, especially C. S. Lewis's, Collins judged his objections superficial and eventually found faith more rational than atheism for him.",
      "completeLockedSourceExcerpt": "questions and quickly found myself in theological quarters and thought i would be able to shoot down all their arguments to my surprise and particularly influenced by the writings of c.s lewis i realized that my arguments were actually pretty superficial and ultimately over a two year period with a lot of kicking and screaming came to the conclusion that faith was more rational",
      "assessmentRationaleWithoutScores": "Strongest feature: Collins presents conversion as the result of prolonged comparative reflection rather than sudden certainty, acknowledging his initial hostility and the substantial revision of his own objections. Principal limitation: Because the theological arguments, rival explanations, and standards of comparison are absent, readers receive sincere testimony about a reasoning process but cannot reproduce or evaluate the inference that faith became more rational. Live burden: Collins must translate the intellectual biography into public premises showing why Lewis’s case outperformed atheism rather than merely documenting that it persuaded him personally."
    },
    {
      "moveId": "con-simple-to-complex-presupposition",
      "side": "con",
      "sectionTitle": "personal routes and epistemic scope",
      "role": "Constructive",
      "currentDescription": "Dawkins acknowledges that both speakers bring presuppositions, and concludes that his evolutionary formation inclines him toward explaining complex things through simpler beginnings.",
      "lockedProposition": "Dawkins acknowledges that both speakers approach the issue with presuppositions and that his is shaped by attraction to explaining complex things through simpler ones.",
      "completeLockedSourceExcerpt": "part of it i i suppose um perhaps we both come at it from with a with with a bit of um emotional not emotionally the wrong word a bit a bit of presupposition um as a as somebody who's deeply steeped in evolution um i am kind of in love with the idea that it's possible to explain complex things in terms of simple things",
      "assessmentRationaleWithoutScores": "Strongest feature: Dawkins candidly identifies his own methodological attraction and grants that both speakers approach the evidence with prior orientations, improving the transparency of the ensuing complexity argument. Principal limitation: Evolution’s success as one simple-to-complex explanation does not establish that every ultimate explanation must share that structure, and describing the preference as partly presuppositional reduces its independent argumentative force. Live burden: Dawkins must convert the disclosed attraction into a defended principle of comparative explanation and show that it applies coherently beyond biological objects to fundamental reality."
    },
    {
      "moveId": "pro-science-cannot-prove-transcendent",
      "side": "pro",
      "sectionTitle": "personal routes and epistemic scope",
      "role": "Direct reply",
      "currentDescription": "Collins concludes that science may contribute evidence concerning God but cannot alone prove or disprove an extra-natural reality using tools designed to investigate nature.",
      "lockedProposition": "If God exists outside nature, science may provide pieces of evidence but cannot by itself prove or disprove God's existence.",
      "completeLockedSourceExcerpt": "i think if there is something outside of nature and if god exists god is definitely outside of nature then the tools that we use to investigate nature which is science and it's really good at that may not be adequate for this so in that regard i don't think it is a scientific question i think you can explore possible bits of evidence but i don't think you can prove yes or no to the god question solely with the tools",
      "assessmentRationaleWithoutScores": "Strongest feature: Collins draws a careful three-part distinction among investigating nature, gathering indirect evidential pieces, and conclusively proving or disproving a proposed transcendent reality. Principal limitation: Defining God as outside nature partly builds methodological insulation into the hypothesis, and the response does not specify how indirect evidence could confirm God while leaving possible disconfirmation sufficiently meaningful. Live burden: Collins must preserve evidential accountability by explaining which observations favor or challenge his cumulative case, despite denying that science alone can settle the question."
    },
    {
      "moveId": "con-god-as-scientific-question",
      "side": "con",
      "sectionTitle": "personal routes and epistemic scope",
      "role": "Constructive",
      "currentDescription": "Dawkins concludes that God’s existence is both enormously consequential and scientifically assessable, although he does not specify the observations or criteria that would adjudicate it.",
      "lockedProposition": "Dawkins regards God's existence as the largest question one could ask and as a scientific question.",
      "completeLockedSourceExcerpt": "i don't think this is a trivial question i i think that whether or not there is a god is the biggest question you could ask biggest scientist actually it's a scientific question francis may disagree with that um i think of it as a scientific question",
      "assessmentRationaleWithoutScores": "Strongest feature: Dawkins treats the God question as serious, meaningful, and potentially answerable rather than dismissing it as empty, thereby placing competing claims under evidential scrutiny. Principal limitation: Calling it a scientific question remains ambiguous without testable predictions, possible falsifiers, scope conditions, or a distinction between a hypothesis’s observable consequences and its complete disciplinary classification. Live burden: Dawkins must specify how scientific evidence could discriminate the relevant God hypothesis and explain what would count against his no-need conclusion."
    },
    {
      "moveId": "pro-evolution-compatible-with-plan",
      "side": "pro",
      "sectionTitle": "evolution and biological design",
      "role": "Constructive",
      "currentDescription": "Collins concludes that evolution’s powerful explanation of biodiversity does not exclude divine purpose, because mechanism and a plan operating at a deeper level are compatible.",
      "lockedProposition": "Evolution powerfully explains biological diversity, but that explanatory success does not itself exclude a divine plan; it moves the proposed plan to a deeper level.",
      "completeLockedSourceExcerpt": "but certainly uh evolution is incredibly powerful as an explanatory science to understand the amazing diversity of creatures that we see around us and that we know have lived in the past but i don't see how that in any way excludes the possibility that there was a plan it's just for me that steps further back",
      "assessmentRationaleWithoutScores": "Strongest feature: Collins fully credits evolutionary science and makes the logically limited inference that a complete natural mechanism need not contradict a deeper purposive interpretation, directly protecting his central compatibility burden. Principal limitation: Compatibility establishes possibility, not probability or explanatory improvement, and the passage supplies no independent reason to infer that such a plan actually exists behind the accepted mechanism. Live burden: Collins must move from non-exclusion to comparative warrant while answering Dawkins’s contention that a process already sufficient to generate apparent design makes the designer explanatorily idle."
    },
    {
      "moveId": "con-evolution-waste-and-redundancy",
      "side": "con",
      "sectionTitle": "evolution and biological design",
      "role": "Direct reply",
      "currentDescription": "Dawkins concludes that selection makes God superfluous because it is wasteful for intentional design and possesses the crucial capacity to operate without divine direction.",
      "lockedProposition": "Natural selection is an implausibly wasteful route for an intending creator and, because it could occur without God, makes God superfluous.",
      "completeLockedSourceExcerpt": "i think i would not use such a a wasteful long drawn-out process i think i just go for it i mean why would you choose um why would you choose natural selection uh which has the possibly unfortunate property that it could have come about without you why would god have chosen a mechanism to unfold his design he chose the very mechanism which actually makes him superfluous",
      "assessmentRationaleWithoutScores": "Strongest feature: Dawkins directly attacks Collins’s “elegant means” proposal at two distinct points, contrasting expected intentional efficiency with a mechanism whose autonomous operation already accounts for the outcome. Principal limitation: The waste objection relies on uncertain expectations about divine preferences, and explanatory sufficiency does not logically exclude a creator who values lawful development, creaturely independence, or goods unavailable through immediate manufacture. Live burden: Dawkins must ground his strongest case in redundancy rather than speculative divine psychology and explain why an unnecessary hypothesis lacks rational support rather than merely lacking scientific necessity."
    },
    {
      "moveId": "pro-evolution-as-divine-means",
      "side": "pro",
      "sectionTitle": "evolution and biological design",
      "role": "Constructive",
      "currentDescription": "Collins concludes that a timeless God could elegantly employ evolution to produce conscious creatures while knowing its outcome without repeatedly intervening in natural history.",
      "lockedProposition": "If a timeless God intended conscious creatures, evolution could be an elegant means whose outcome God knew without intervening in each step.",
      "completeLockedSourceExcerpt": "wouldn't evolution have been a very elegant way to do so and if god who's in my sense outside of space and time and therefore doesn't require a way to have been begun used this process and knew full well how it would happen because of this ability to be outside of time i think that's just an amazing concept",
      "assessmentRationaleWithoutScores": "Strongest feature: Collins offers an internally intelligible providential model in which evolution is not reluctantly tolerated but becomes the elegant means by which an intended outcome develops under stable natural processes. Principal limitation: Timeless foreknowledge, divine intention, and the desirability of this route are introduced as theological possibilities without evidence that distinguishes them from an entirely natural history or establishes their comparative plausibility. Live burden: Collins must show why elegance supports agency rather than reflecting his prior interpretation, while answering waste, suffering, and the fact that selection operates without detectable supervision."
    },
    {
      "moveId": "con-selection-suffering",
      "side": "con",
      "sectionTitle": "evolution and biological design",
      "role": "Constructive",
      "currentDescription": "Dawkins concludes that natural selection is not benign because competition systematically involves starvation, predation, disease, and death, although he treats this as secondary.",
      "lockedProposition": "From a human perspective, natural selection is non-benign: competition brings starvation, predation, disease, and suffering, though Dawkins calls this a less important argument.",
      "completeLockedSourceExcerpt": "we are human uh and and um the the the suffering which which comes from the fact that it's all about competition it's all about is evading starvation the ones that die are the ones who are starved to death or eaten by predators uh consumed by disease um it's it's it's not a benign process at all but that's not a very important argument i just was it",
      "assessmentRationaleWithoutScores": "Strongest feature: Dawkins names concrete biological costs of selection and carefully limits the conclusion to its non-benign character, expressly ranking the point below his principal explanatory argument. Principal limitation: The examples demonstrate suffering but do not alone establish that a good creator could have no sufficient reason for a lawful evolutionary world, nor do they compare feasible alternatives and their associated goods. Live burden: Dawkins must connect the documented harms to a discriminating expectation under the relevant theism while respecting his concession that suffering is not a logical disproof."
    },
    {
      "moveId": "pro-timelessness-answers-duration",
      "side": "pro",
      "sectionTitle": "evolution and biological design",
      "role": "Direct reply",
      "currentDescription": "Collins concludes that evolution’s immense duration is no divine cost because a God outside time knows the outcome without experiencing the process as prolonged.",
      "lockedProposition": "Evolution's duration is not an objection from the perspective of a timeless God for whom the process is effectively instantaneous and its outcome known.",
      "completeLockedSourceExcerpt": "one is that i don't think the fact that it took a long time should trouble us particularly from god's perspective uh yeah it's a long time for us but again in this view where god is pretty much outside of space and time it's a blink of an eye with a full knowledge of where the outcome would occur",
      "assessmentRationaleWithoutScores": "Strongest feature: Collins precisely isolates the temporal component of Dawkins’s waste objection and explains why elapsed human time need not count as delay or inconvenience for an atemporal creator. Principal limitation: Describing timeless existence as a “blink” imports temporal imagery into the proposed condition, while the reply leaves evolutionary suffering, failed lineages, redundancy, and the mechanism’s autonomous sufficiency substantially untouched. Live burden: Collins must distinguish temporal duration from the broader charge of waste and show that timelessness is independently coherent and relevant rather than an exemption built into the hypothesis."
    },
    {
      "moveId": "con-bottom-up-explanation-removes-design",
      "side": "con",
      "sectionTitle": "evolution and biological design",
      "role": "Direct reply",
      "currentDescription": "Because evolution builds complexity, elegance, and apparent design from simplicity, Dawkins concludes that reintroducing design at the beginning betrays an explanation that makes a designer unnecessary.",
      "lockedProposition": "Because evolution builds complexity and apparent design from simplicity, adding design at the beginning betrays the bottom-up explanation that made a designer unnecessary.",
      "completeLockedSourceExcerpt": "under really understand that the evolutionary process starts with with simplicity and builds up to complexity and elegance and beauty and uh strong illusion of design then to smuggle design in again at the beginning is to betray the entire enterprise which you've spent so long working out and building up the enterprise has been we now understand that you don't actually need a designer",
      "assessmentRationaleWithoutScores": "Strongest feature: Dawkins states the central Darwinian inference with exceptional clarity: gradual processes build complexity and apparent design from simpler beginnings, so a designer no longer performs the work once assigned to it. Principal limitation: Calling deeper purpose a betrayal overstates what mechanism establishes, because explanatory redundancy within biology does not logically exclude providence or determine whether independent cosmic and experiential evidence supports God. Live burden: Dawkins must defend the move as a no-need conclusion rather than an impossibility claim and address Collins’s redirection toward the laws and initial conditions enabling evolution."
    },
    {
      "moveId": "pro-laws-remain-unexplained",
      "side": "pro",
      "sectionTitle": "evolution and biological design",
      "role": "Direct reply",
      "currentDescription": "Collins concludes that Darwinian explanation leaves a deeper question unanswered because the physical laws enabling evolution still require an account of their origin.",
      "lockedProposition": "Collins argues that explaining evolution through the laws of physics leaves unanswered where those laws came from.",
      "completeLockedSourceExcerpt": "but you said that well it's happened just because of the laws of physics i want to take this back to that step where did those come from well",
      "assessmentRationaleWithoutScores": "Strongest feature: Collins concedes the bottom-up evolutionary account rather than resisting it, then cleanly distinguishes explaining biological complexity under physical laws from explaining why those enabling laws obtain. Principal limitation: A genuine residual question is not yet evidence for divine authorship, and the brief challenge offers neither a comparative causal argument nor a reason that the laws require an external personal source. Live burden: Collins must convert the foundational question into positive, discriminating warrant while meeting the objection that a creator may relocate rather than resolve the explanatory demand."
    },

from ignorance","type":"fallacy","decision":"rejected","rationale":"The move reports only that science did not help Collins answer certain existential questions; it does not infer that God or theology is therefore true. The assessment explicitly treats it as a restrained scope claim, so the catalog definition is not materially instantiated."},{"moveId":"pro-comparative-inquiry-supported-faith","label":"Appeal to authority","type":"fallacy","decision":"rejected","rationale":"Although Collins identifies C. S. Lewis as influential, he does not say Lewis's status settles the issue. The assessment criticizes the omission of Lewis's arguments and comparative standards, which is underdevelopment rather than reliance on authority as proof."},{"moveId":"pro-comparative-inquiry-supported-faith","label":"Subjective validation","type":"bias","decision":"rejected","rationale":"Collins gives autobiographical testimony about what persuaded him, but he does not present personal resonance as public verification of Christianity. The assessment asks him to supply reproducible premises; that missing public argument alone does not establish the defined bias."},{"moveId":"con-simple-to-complex-presupposition","label":"Belief bias","type":"bias","decision":"rejected","rationale":"Dawkins openly describes an attraction shaped by evolutionary study, but he does not claim that this attraction establishes the ultimate explanatory principle. The assessment treats the disclosure as transparent but weak, not as substitution of believability for validity."},{"moveId":"pro-science-cannot-prove-transcendent","label":"Special pleading","type":"fallacy","decision":"accepted","rationale":"Collins defines God as outside nature and therefore beyond science's capacity to prove or disprove, while still allowing scientific evidence to contribute to belief. The assessment identifies this built-in insulation and the unexplained asymmetry between confirmation and disconfirmation."},{"moveId":"pro-evolution-compatible-with-plan","label":"Argument from ignorance","type":"fallacy","decision":"rejected","rationale":"Collins argues only that evolution does not logically exclude a deeper plan, not that non-exclusion proves such a plan exists. The assessment expressly distinguishes compatibility from probability, so the move does not treat lack of disproof as positive proof."},{"moveId":"pro-evolution-as-divine-means","label":"Confirmation bias","type":"bias","decision":"rejected","rationale":"The description of evolution as elegant fits Collins's prior theological interpretation, but the move does not display selective evidence handling or discount identified contrary evidence. The assessment notes a lack of discrimination, which is insufficient to infer confirmation bias."},{"moveId":"pro-timelessness-answers-duration","label":"Special pleading","type":"fallacy","decision":"rejected","rationale":"Atemporality supplies a relevant category-based reason why elapsed time would not burden God, so this is not yet an unprincipled exception. The assessment questions coherence and independence but does not establish that Collins applies a knowingly different standard without reason."},{"moveId":"pro-laws-remain-unexplained","label":"Argument from ignorance","type":"fallacy","decision":"rejected","rationale":"Collins asks where the enabling physical laws came from without asserting in this move that their unexplained origin proves divine authorship. The assessment identifies a residual question and warns against a later unsupported inference, not an ignorance inference already made."},{"moveId":"pro-transcendent-mind-exceeds-concepts","label":"Special pleading","type":"fallacy","decision":"rejected","rationale":"The claim that ordinary models may inadequately describe a transcendent mind offers a principled difference in subject matter. The assessment warns that asymmetry would arise if positive claims remained admissible while criticism was excluded, but does not find that full asymmetry established here."},{"moveId":"con-divine-simplicity-implausible","label":"Begging the question","type":"fallacy","decision":"rejected","rationale":"Dawkins's inference from sophisticated capability to complexity is insufficiently defended and may use the wrong complexity metric, but it is offered as a substantive premise rather than merely restating the conclusion. A disputed premise is not necessarily circular."},{"moveId":"pro-multiverse-also-evidential-leap","label":"Ambiguity effect","type":"bias","decision":"rejected","rationale":"Collins emphasizes the multiverse's experimental inaccessibility, but he acknowledges its observer-selection explanation and calls both alternatives evidential leaps. The assessment faults an incomplete evidential comparison, not a demonstrated preference caused by ambiguity itself."},{"moveId":"pro-timeless-god-stops-regress","label":"Special pleading","type":"fallacy","decision":"rejected","rationale":"An atemporal being would not require a temporal beginning for the same reason temporally originated beings do, providing a relevant proposed distinction. The assessment says this premise needs independent defense but does not establish an exception lacking any principled basis."},{"moveId":"con-constant-sensitivity","label":"Appeal to authority","type":"fallacy","decision":"rejected","rationale":"Dawkins mentions physicists' agreement but also supplies the evidential chain involving galaxies, stars, chemistry, and life. The assessment criticizes documentation and overbreadth, not reliance on expert status as though it alone settled fine-tuning."},{"moveId":"pro-priors-mediate-explanations","label":"Confirmation bias","type":"bias","decision":"rejected","rationale":"Collins correctly observes that priors mediate underdetermined comparisons, but does not here selectively manipulate evidence to protect his own view. The assessment warns that unspecified priors leave the judgment vulnerable to starting commitments, which is not proof of the defined bias."},{"moveId":"con-multiverse-not-ad-hoc","label":"Appeal to authority","type":"fallacy","decision":"rejected","rationale":"Dawkins invokes reputable inflationary physics secondhand, but repeatedly qualifies his expertise and treats the point tentatively rather than settled by prestige. The assessment demands substantiation; it does not find authority functioning as decisive proof."},{"moveId":"pro-human-capacities-fit-purpose","label":"Confirmation bias","type":"bias","decision":"accepted","rationale":"Collins says the universe has exactly the expected properties by selecting morality, love, beauty, and religious seeking while omitting parasites, disasters, disease, extinction, and moral failure. The assessment expressly identifies this one-sided evidential selection."},{"moveId":"pro-rare-miracles-convey-message","label":"Special pleading","type":"fallacy","decision":"rejected","rationale":"Collins gives a stated principle for the exception: rare interventions communicate pivotal messages while ordinary regularity remains intact. The principle may be evidentially unsupported or morally inadequate, but it is a principled reason rather than an unexplained exemption."},{"moveId":"pro-constant-intervention-destroys-order","label":"Red herring","type":"fallacy","decision":"accepted","rationale":"Dawkins's challenge concerns selective intervention and bounded rescues, but Collins redirects it to intervention at every hurricane and the chaos of constant suspension. The assessment explicitly notes that this extreme scenario leaves the bounded-intervention challenge unanswered."},{"moveId":"pro-nobility-exceeds-misfiring-description","label":"Belief bias","type":"bias","decision":"accepted","rationale":"Collins treats the evolutionary account as inadequate because describing noble altruism as a misfiring feels evaluatively troubling, although nobility is compatible with a natural causal history. The assessment identifies this mistaken opposition between moral significance and explanation."},{"moveId":"pro-morality-signposts-holy-god","label":"Argument from ignorance","type":"fallacy","decision":"accepted","rationale":"Collins's stated difficulty seeing obligation as purely evolutionary becomes a signpost toward a holy, interested God without a completed positive bridge. The assessment notes that naturalistic rivals are insufficiently compared and that the theistic inference remains incomplete."},{"moveId":"con-moral-terms-need-no-spirit","label":"Begging the question","type":"fallacy","decision":"accepted","rationale":"Defining good as what good people do and evil as what bad people do presupposes the very moral classifications needing explanation. The assessment explicitly calls the formulation circular and notes that it supplies no independent standard for identifying good people."},{"moveId":"pro-beauty-lacks-obvious-fitness-value","label":"Argument from ignorance","type":"fallacy","decision":"accepted","rationale":"Collins treats the absence of an obvious evolutionary benefit as reason to resist a natural account of mathematical, musical, and natural beauty. The assessment identifies several unexcluded natural mechanisms, making the reasoning materially depend on what has not been shown."},{"moveId":"con-beauty-has-natural-analogy","label":"Equivocation","type":"fallacy","decision":"accepted","rationale":"Dawkins moves from peahen mate preference to the much broader human category of beauty without preserving a demonstrated common meaning across music, mathematics, landscapes, and abstraction. The assessment expressly flags this potentially loose cross-species usage."},{"moveId":"pro-joy-suggests-transcendence","label":"Subjective validation","type":"bias","decision":"accepted","rationale":"Collins treats a personally significant, fleeting feeling of something more as experiential support for transcendence. The assessment states that the seeming does not verify a transcendent object and warns against relying on intensity or personal meaning alone."}],"acceptedTags":[{"moveId":"pro-science-cannot-prove-transcendent","label":"Special pleading","type":"fallacy","url":"https://logfall.com/fallacies/special-pleading/","context":"Collins places God outside nature and therefore beyond science's capacity for proof or disproof, while retaining the possibility that scientific observations can contribute affirmative evidence to his cumulative case.","rationale":"This materially applies different evidential access to the God hypothesis without specifying a principled symmetry between possible confirmation and disconfirmation, matching the assessment's concern about methodological insulation."},{"moveId":"pro-human-capacities-fit-purpose","label":"Confirmation bias","type":"bias","url":"https://cogbias.site/biases/confirmation-bias/","context":"Collins highlights moral responsibility, love, beauty, knowledge of good and evil, and religious seeking as exactly what divine purpose predicts, while making a universal claim about the universe's properties.","rationale":"The assessment finds that this interpretation selects hospitable evidence while omitting extensive natural and moral counterevidence, materially instantiating one-sided interpretation in favor of the existing theistic view."},{"moveId":"pro-constant-intervention-destroys-order","label":"Red herring","type":"fallacy","url":"https://logfall.com/fallacies/red-herring/","context":"Asked why God selectively performs revelatory miracles but does not prevent severe harms, Collins answers by imagining divine intervention every time a hurricane occurs and the resulting chaos.","rationale":"The extreme constant-intervention scenario diverts from the live bounded-rescue challenge. As the assessment explains, carefully limited rescues need not destroy natural order, so the original selection problem remains unanswered."},{"moveId":"pro-nobility-exceeds-misfiring-description","label":"Belief bias","type":"bias","url":"https://cogbias.site/biases/belief-bias/","context":"Collins says it bothers him to characterize exceptionally noble altruism as an evolutionary mechanism misfiring and treats that morally unattractive characterization as a reason the explanation is inadequate.","rationale":"The perceived nobility and desirability of the conduct do not bear on whether its causal explanation is valid. The assessment specifically identifies Collins's mistaken opposition between moral significance and natural history."},{"moveId":"pro-morality-signposts-holy-god","label":"Argument from ignorance","type":"fallacy","url":"https://logfall.com/fallacies/argument-from-ignorance/","context":"Collins says he has great difficulty seeing felt moral obligation as a purely evolutionary consequence and then treats that unresolved naturalistic explanation as a signpost toward a holy God interested in humanity.","rationale":"The positive theistic bridge is not supplied, while evolutionary and cultural rivals remain insufficiently compared. Thus inability to see an adequate natural explanation materially carries the proposed signpost inference."},{"moveId":"con-moral-terms-need-no-spirit","label":"Begging the question","type":"fallacy","url":"https://logfall.com/fallacies/begging-the-question/","context":"Dawkins proposes that good is what good people do and evil is what bad people do as an allegedly sufficient naturalistic account of moral terms without an independent supernatural moral entity.","rationale":"The proposal identifies good people only by presupposing goodness and then uses their conduct to define goodness. It therefore smuggles the required moral standard into its premise exactly as the assessment's circularity criticism states."},{"moveId":"pro-beauty-lacks-obvious-fitness-value","label":"Argument from ignorance","type":"fallacy","url":"https://logfall.com/fallacies/argument-from-ignorance/","context":"Collins argues that mathematical, musical, and natural beauty resist the proposed natural analogy because these experiences do not seem to possess much obvious evolutionary benefit despite their significance.","rationale":"A lack of an obvious direct fitness benefit is used against natural explanation even though cognitive byproducts, learning, social coordination, culture, and indirect benefits remain open, as the assessment specifically observes."},{"moveId":"con-beauty-has-natural-analogy","label":"Equivocation","type":"fallacy","url":"https://logfall.com/fallacies/equivocation/","context":"Dawkins uses the same term, beauty, first for peahen mating preference that shapes peacock appearance and then for the broad human aesthetic capacities under dispute, claiming an analogous explanation.","rationale":"The argument gains force by sliding between a narrow sexual preference and human responses to music, mathematics, landscapes, and abstraction without establishing that the operative concept remains the same across those domains."},{"moveId":"pro-joy-suggests-transcendence","label":"Subjective validation","type":"bias","url":"https://cogbias.site/biases/subjective-validation/","context":"Collins describes a fleeting, deeply meaningful personal sense that there is something more beyond ordinary life and treats the felt significance of this Lewisian joy as experiential support for transcendence.","rationale":"The move gives evidential weight to the experience because it feels personally resonant and transcendent, although that seeming does not verify an external transcendent object and remains compatible with psychological and neural accounts."}]}
